file_description: Well Characteristics - Static well metadata and geometry
data_format: WIDE format - one row per well (static data)

field_descriptions.well_name: Official well designation (sigla) - unique identifier following naming convention
field_descriptions.well_id: Numeric well identifier in government database
field_descriptions.field_name: Reservoir/field name (yacimiento) where well is located
field_descriptions.basin: Sedimentary basin - major geological province (e.g., Neuquina, Golfo San Jorge)
field_descriptions.surface_elevation_m: Ground level elevation above mean sea level in meters
field_descriptions.total_depth_m: Total measured depth of well from surface to bottom in meters
field_descriptions.formation_depth_m: Depth to top of producing formation in meters
field_descriptions.well_location_geojson: Well surface location in GeoJSON Point format with coordinates
field_descriptions.resource_subtype: Specific unconventional play type if applicable

classification_descriptions.exploration: Wildcat well drilled to discover new oil/gas accumulations in unproven areas
classification_descriptions.production_development: Well drilled to produce from known/proven reservoir - development drilling
classification_descriptions.appraisal: Well drilled after discovery to evaluate reservoir size, productivity, and economics
classification_descriptions.delineation_stepout: Well drilled to define lateral extent and boundaries of discovered reservoir
classification_descriptions.injection: Well drilled or converted for fluid injection - water, gas, or CO2
classification_descriptions.abandonment: Well being permanently plugged and abandoned per regulations

resource_type_descriptions.conventional: Porous and permeable reservoir rock - oil/gas flows naturally or with conventional lift. Permeability typically >1 millidarcy (mD).
resource_type_descriptions.unconventional: Low permeability reservoir requiring hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling. Permeability typically <0.1 mD. Includes tight gas/oil, shale, and coalbed methane.
resource_type_descriptions.tight_gas_oil: Low permeability sandstone or carbonate reservoirs - permeability 0.001-0.1 mD. Requires hydraulic fracturing but not as extensive as shale.
resource_type_descriptions.shale_gas: Gas trapped in organic-rich shale formations (e.g., Vaca Muerta). Ultra-low permeability (<0.001 mD), requires multi-stage hydraulic fracturing in horizontal wells.
resource_type_descriptions.shale_oil: Oil in shale formations - same characteristics as shale gas but liquid hydrocarbons. Vaca Muerta formation is Argentina's major shale oil play.
resource_type_descriptions.coalbed_methane: Gas adsorbed onto coal surfaces - requires dewatering to reduce pressure and release gas. Different production mechanism than conventional gas.

unit_notes.meters: All depth and elevation measurements in meters
unit_notes.decimal_degrees: Latitude/longitude in decimal degrees format (WGS84 datum assumed)
unit_notes.coordinate_system: Local projected coordinates - system varies by region/province
unit_notes.geojson_format: Point geometry with [longitude, latitude] coordinate pair

technical_notes.depth_conventions: Total depth = measured depth along wellbore. True vertical depth (TVD) may be less for deviated/horizontal wells.
technical_notes.formation_depth: Depth to top of primary producing interval - may have multiple zones
technical_notes.vaca_muerta_importance: Vaca Muerta formation in Neuquina basin is world-class shale play - most unconventional wells target this formation
technical_notes.conventional_basins: Golfo San Jorge and Austral basins are primarily conventional. Neuquina basin has both conventional and unconventional (Vaca Muerta).
